name: Brow lift / brow bone augmentation
summary: Surgical or injectable ways to raise the eyebrows or reshape the brow ridge; established for brow ptosis, while bone augmentation for a stronger brow has little published evidence outside reconstructive and gender-affirming work.
lead: A brow lift (also forehead lift, browplasty or browpexy) is a cosmetic or reconstructive procedure that raises a low or drooping eyebrow and may soften forehead lines . Techniques include endoscopic, coronal, direct, temporal, hairline and transblepharoplasty approaches, plus non-surgical options such as botulinum toxin and soft tissue fillers . A published review of ten popular techniques concluded that none is completely satisfactory because of limited effectiveness, longevity or complications .
claims: A brow lift can fix a low or tired-looking brow position as part of a wider facial overhaul.
Brow bone implants or augmentation can create a stronger, more masculine brow ridge.
Botulinum toxin can raise or reshape the brow without surgery.
Surgery abroad, such as in Turkey, is a cost-effective route for brow and facial procedures.

name: Facial masculinization surgery
summary: Gender-affirming craniofacial surgery that squares the jaw, projects the chin and builds up the forehead and brow; the literature is mostly reviews and case reports, and looksmaxxers borrow the techniques for appearance goals.
lead: Facial masculinization surgery (FMS) is a group of reconstructive and aesthetic procedures that make facial features more masculine, mainly performed as gender-affirming surgery for trans men and transmasculine people . Procedures include forehead augmentation to create a less rounded forehead and stronger brow ridge, jaw and chin augmentation, and a rib-cartilage procedure to enlarge the Adam's apple first reported in 2017 .
claims: Skeletal forehead and brow work can masculinize the upper face.
Jaw and chin implants or fillers are a route to a more masculine lower face.
Non-bony options such as fillers or fat can contour the forehead.

name: Hair transplant (FUE/FUT)
summary: Surgical relocation of follicles from the back of the scalp to thinning or bald areas; an established, durable procedure that depends on donor supply and surgeon skill.
lead: Hair transplantation is a surgical procedure in which hair follicles from a donor region, typically the back and sides of the scalp, are relocated to areas of hair loss . It is used mainly for androgenetic alopecia (male and female pattern hair loss), and also for some scarring alopecias and to correct trauma or prior surgery . Modern practice is built on follicular unit transplantation, in which naturally occurring groups of one to four hairs are used as grafts .
claims: Transplant success rates above 95 percent are overstated and results are a gamble.
Hair transplant is a good last-resort option for someone who expects to go bald young.
Turkey clinics offer comparable results at much lower prices.
Timing matters: getting a transplant very young may cause problems as loss progresses.

name: Beard transplant
summary: Follicular unit grafts moved to the jaw and cheeks to fill patchy or absent facial hair; described in surgical reviews as a refined procedure, with outcome data limited to surgeon-reported series.
lead: Beard transplantation is the surgical relocation of hair follicles, usually taken from the scalp, to areas of the face where facial hair is thin, patchy or absent. It sits within hair restoration surgery alongside eyebrow, sideburn and eyelash transplantation .

name: Eyebrow transplant
summary: Hair grafts placed to build denser or reshaped eyebrows; small surgeon series report high satisfaction, with no controlled trials.
lead: Eyebrow transplantation is a hair restoration procedure in which follicular units are moved into the eyebrow to increase density, fill sparse areas or reshape the brow . Reviews describe it as having become popular, and follicular unit extraction (FUE) as the most popular technique .
claims: An eyebrow transplant can make brows thicker, longer or reshaped.
A transplant could be a lower-risk way to lower the brow than surgery or botulinum toxin.

name: Facial fillers (jawline/chin/cheek)
summary: Injectable hyaluronic acid or similar fillers used to add projection to the jaw, chin and cheeks without surgery; temporary and adjustable, with rare but serious vascular risks.
lead: Dermal fillers are injectable materials placed in the skin or deeper tissue to restore or add volume . For the jawline, chin and cheeks they are used to sharpen the jaw angle, project the chin and raise cheek contour, an approach sometimes called facial balancing . Hyaluronic acid (HA) is the most widely used filler material and is biodegradable; other materials include calcium hydroxylapatite and poly-L-lactic acid .
claims: Jawline filler gives a visible jaw improvement without surgery.
Filler maintenance is an affordable alternative to implants.
Filler must be dissolved if unwanted; it does not leave on its own.
Jawline filler is low risk.

name: Calcium hydroxylapatite filler (Radiesse)
summary: A dense, collagen-stimulating injectable filler used for cheek, jaw and chin structure; studied mainly in ageing faces, with little trial data on young-adult contouring goals.
lead: Calcium hydroxylapatite filler, sold most prominently as Radiesse (Merz Aesthetics), is an injectable soft-tissue filler made of calcium hydroxylapatite microspheres suspended in a carboxymethylcellulose gel . It is classed as a biostimulatory filler because, besides giving immediate volume, it is reported to induce new collagen, elastin and blood vessel formation in the surrounding tissue .
claims: High G prime filler can mimic bone and sharpen the jaw or chin without surgery.
Hydroxyapatite is the closest material to real bone and the best facial implant material.

name: Black-market / DIY fillers
summary: Filler bought outside regulated channels and injected without a clinician; the practice exists on forums, and the main risks are those regulators and reviewers attach to all fillers, with no safeguards.
lead: Black-market or DIY filler is the practice of buying injectable dermal filler outside regulated medical supply and administering it to oneself, as described on looksmaxxing forums. It overlaps with the broader topic of unlicensed injection of fat-dissolving agents and botulinum toxin, which some users discuss in the same threads .
claims: Filler can be self-administered safely if the injector studies anatomy and follows safety rules.
Filler gives a cheap way to add jaw or chin structure that mimics surgery.

name: Masseter Botox
summary: Botulinum toxin injected into the jaw muscle to slim a wide lower face; reasonably studied for muscle prominence, but temporary, and a 2025 trial is the main data on bone effects.
lead: Masseter Botox is the injection of botulinum toxin type A into the masseter muscle, the thick muscle that closes the jaw . It is used to treat masseter muscle hypertrophy or prominence, a benign enlargement that can widen the lower face, and to treat bruxism (teeth grinding) and jaw pain . In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to slim the lower face and soften a boxy jaw outline.
claims: Masseter Botox slims the lower face and gives hollows.
It should be reserved for bruxism or extreme cases.
The toxin may weaken the jawbone.

name: Lip filler
summary: Injected gel that adds lip volume and definition; well documented in trials, temporary, and a minor lever in forum rating systems that put more weight on mouth width.
lead: Lip filler, or lip augmentation with fillers, is the injection of a soft-tissue filler, most commonly a hyaluronic acid (HA) gel, to increase lip volume, enhance the vermilion border or improve the ratio between the upper and lower lip . Perioral tissues are among the first to show ageing, and reviews say many patients seek perioral fillers as their first cosmetic treatment .
claims: Fuller lips are a cheap, easy improvement.
Lip filler is cope; mouth width relative to nose width matters more.

name: Under-eye filler (tear trough)
summary: Filler placed in the hollow under the eyes to soften shadowing; widely used and fairly well described, but a high-skill area where delayed swelling, lumps and rare vision-threatening events are documented.
lead: Under-eye filler, or tear trough filler, is the injection of a dermal filler, most often hyaluronic acid (HA), into the tear trough, the depression running from the inner corner of the eye toward the cheek, to soften hollowing and shadowing under the eyes . Reviews state that dermal fillers can camouflage tear trough deformity and orbital fat pseudoherniation .
claims: Tear trough filler gives a noticeable improvement without a plastic look and with little downtime.
Tear trough filler is low risk.

name: Liposuction / chin lipo
summary: Surgical suction removal of fat, including under the chin and neck; common and well studied overall, with permanent fat-cell removal but contour irregularities and rare serious complications.
lead: Liposuction, also called lipoplasty or suction-assisted lipectomy, is a surgical procedure in which fat is removed from beneath the skin by suction through a cannula . Submental (chin) liposuction targets fat under the chin and along the neck, and in looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to define the jawline and neck angle.
claims: Liposuction permanently removes fat from the jaw and neck.
Liposuction is a low-risk shortcut compared with dieting.

name: Otoplasty (ear pinning)
summary: Surgery that sets protruding ears closer to the head; a long-established procedure with high reported satisfaction, usually discussed in looksmaxxing as a cheap add-on.
lead: Otoplasty, commonly called ear pinning, is plastic surgery of the outer ear (auricle). It is most often performed to correct prominent ears, sometimes called "bat ears", which result from an underdeveloped antihelical fold, an enlarged conchal bowl, or a protruding earlobe.  The same family of operations is also used for congenital malformations such as constricted ears, Stahl's deformity and cryptotia, and for ear reconstruction.
claims: Otoplasty is a "high roi" add-on to jaw surgery
Pinning ears back can raise facial masculinity more than custom implants
Otoplasty can leave deformities such as outward lobes or downward upper helix
Teenagers are poor candidates because of scarring

name: Gold thread lift
summary: Implanting fine gold threads under the skin for wrinkles and 'lift'; documented mainly through a small clinical series and a growing set of case reports of retained threads.
lead: Gold thread implantation (also called gold thread therapy or gold thread acupuncture) involves inserting fine gold strands under the skin. Published reports describe it in cosmetic contexts such as facial wrinkles and rejuvenation, and in acupuncture-related contexts such as pain relief.

name: PDO thread lift
summary: Absorbable polydioxanone threads inserted under the skin to lift sagging tissue; immediate improvement is reported, but long-term data are thin.
lead: A thread lift is a minimally invasive procedure that uses sutures, often barbed or cogged, inserted under the skin to suspend ptotic (sagging) tissue. PDO (polydioxanone) threads are absorbable and are the most commonly evaluated thread in recent reviews.

name: Fox eye thread lift
summary: A cosmetic-clinic trend using threads to raise the outer brow and eye corner for an upward 'fox eye' tilt; no published study tests threads for this specific look.
lead: 'Fox eyes' refers to an eye appearance with an upward-angled outer corner and lifted brow tail, popularised through social media and aesthetic clinics. A 'fox eye thread lift' is a minimally invasive procedure that uses absorbable threads, commonly polydioxanone, to lift the brow and lateral eye region toward that shape.
claims: Taping the eyes outward at night can create fox eyes
Threads can lift the outer eye into a fox-eye shape

name: Brazilian butt lift
summary: Autologous fat transfer to the buttocks; powerful, well-documented results in surgical reviews, and a procedure with documented deaths that has driven safety changes.
lead: Brazilian butt lift (BBL) is the common name for buttock augmentation using fat transfer, in which a patient's own fat is harvested by liposuction and injected into the gluteal region.  Wikipedia notes that the term probably comes from the Brazilian surgeon Ivo Pitanguy, who pioneered related surgery in the 1960s, while the Venezuelan surgeon Eduardo Krulig described buttock lipoinjection in 1987.
claims: Men have BBL-style equivalents such as buttock augmentation
BBL is a high-impact, transformative surgery

name: Facelift / neck lift
summary: Surgical lifting of the face and neck tissues; the most established anti-aging surgery, with decades of techniques and published complication data.
lead: A facelift, or rhytidectomy, is cosmetic surgery intended to give the face a more youthful appearance, typically by removing excess skin, tightening deeper tissues and redraping the skin of the face and neck. It is commonly combined with eyelid surgery and neck procedures.
claims: A facelift can only be done once or it looks odd
Surgery beats fillers for keeping a lean face
Jaw advancement surgery improves the submental area

name: Fractional laser resurfacing
summary: Clinic laser that treats skin in tiny columns to remodel scars and texture; well studied for scars and photoaging, with real downtime.
lead: Fractional laser resurfacing is a cosmetic and medical procedure in which a laser delivers energy to the skin in a pattern of many microscopic zones, leaving untreated skin between them. It is used for scars (especially atrophic acne scars), wrinkles, sun-damaged skin, stretch marks and uneven texture, and is a form of the broader category of laser skin resurfacing.
claims: Clinic laser resurfacing meaningfully improves scars and skin texture.
Recovery is brutal and needs about a week off.
Lasers and light treatments such as IPL give long-lasting better skin overall.
Laser resurfacing can be safely bundled into multi-procedure trips abroad.

name: Professional microneedling / RF microneedling
summary: Clinic collagen-induction treatment using fine needles, sometimes with radiofrequency; a moderate body of trials for scars and texture, weaker for hair and add-ons.
lead: Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy or skin needling, is a cosmetic procedure in which fine needles repeatedly puncture the skin to trigger a healing response. Professional versions use motorized pens with adjustable needle depth, and radiofrequency (RF) microneedling adds energy delivered through the needles to heat the deeper skin.
claims: Microneedling improves acne scarring if done consistently.
Deeper needling (clinic or home) gives better results.
Microneedling grows denser beard, eyebrow or scalp hair.
Collagen from needling is a 'stress response' and causes aging or scarring.

name: Medical tourism (Turkey/Istanbul/Korea)
summary: Travelling abroad, often to Turkey or South Korea, for cosmetic surgery, hair transplants or dental work at lower prices; reviews flag infection and follow-up-care risks.
lead: Medical tourism is travel abroad to obtain medical treatment. Historically it meant patients from poorer countries seeking care in wealthy ones; more recently it often means patients from high-income countries travelling to lower-cost destinations, usually for surgery, dental work or fertility treatment, with cosmetic surgery a large category.

name: Gastric sleeve
summary: Bariatric operation that removes most of the stomach; well studied for weight loss and diabetes, with documented surgical and nutritional risks.
lead: Sleeve gastrectomy, often called the gastric sleeve, is a bariatric operation usually performed laparoscopically in which a large portion of the stomach is removed along its greater curvature, leaving a narrow tube-shaped stomach.  It is used to treat severe obesity and obesity-related conditions such as type 2 diabetes.

name: Veneers / Turkey teeth
summary: Thin ceramic or composite shells bonded over teeth for a uniform smile; durable in studies, but preparation can remove enamel and the cheap multi-tooth 'Turkey teeth' packages draw scrutiny.
lead: A dental veneer is a layer of material, most often dental porcelain or composite resin, bonded to the front surface of a tooth to change its colour, shape, size or apparent position.  Laminate veneers are mostly cosmetic and cover only the facial surface, while full veneer crowns cover all coronal surfaces.  Multi-tooth cosmetic makeovers are commonly called 'Hollywood smile' treatments, and the term 'Turkey teeth' has become a nickname for veneers or crowns obtained cheaply at dental clinics in Turkey.
claims: Veneers make a face look healthier and more attractive.
Veneers or crowns can fix an underbite.
Dental work in Turkey is a cost-effective way to get veneers.
Preparing teeth for veneers permanently removes enamel.

name: Calf implants
summary: Silicone implants placed in the lower leg to add calf volume; documented in surgical case series with notable complications such as compartment syndrome.
lead: Calf augmentation is a cosmetic and reconstructive surgery that adds volume to the lower leg, most often with silicone implants placed beneath the fascia or muscle, and sometimes with fat grafting.  Indications include thin legs, asymmetry, bodybuilders seeking more muscle size and deformity from injury or illness.

name: Pec / bicep implants
summary: Solid silicone implants that add chest or arm bulk surgically; little independent evidence exists on cosmetic use in healthy men.
lead: Pectoral and bicep implants are solid silicone prostheses placed surgically beneath or around a muscle to make it look larger or more defined. Pectoral implants are the better documented of the two; they are described as prostheses for the reconstruction and aesthetic repair of a man's chest wall , and the use of the same technology for biceps is far less documented in the sources available.

name: Skin bleaching injections (glutathione IV)
summary: IV glutathione sold as whitening drips; reviewers found no evidence that it lightens skin and a regulator has warned against it.
lead: Glutathione is a small antioxidant molecule made naturally by the body. It is promoted, in oral, topical and intravenous (IV) forms, as a skin-lightening agent, and IV or injected versions are sometimes sold as "whitening drips" . Wikipedia describes glutathione as the most common agent taken by mouth to whiten skin .
claims: Glutathione IV lightens skin and clears undertones.

name: Eye color change surgery (keratopigmentation / iris implants)
summary: Surgery to change eye color via implants or corneal pigment; published reports mainly document serious complications.
lead: Eye color change surgery refers to procedures intended to alter the apparent color of healthy eyes. Two approaches are discussed: cosmetic iris implants, such as NewColorIris and BrightOcular, which are placed inside the eye in front of the natural iris, and keratopigmentation, in which pigment is deposited in the cornea .

name: Penis enlargement surgery
summary: Surgical or filler penile enlargement; urology bodies say safety and efficacy are unproven and complications are documented.
lead: Penis enlargement surgery covers surgical and injectable procedures meant to increase penile length or girth, including suspensory ligament release, fat injection or grafting, dermal fillers and silicone or PMMA injection . Wikipedia states it is not medically indicated except for micropenis .

name: Bonesmashing
summary: Hitting your own facial bones to reshape them; no study supports it and surgeons warn of fractures and nerve damage.
lead: Bonesmashing (also bone smashing or face hammering) is a looksmaxxing practice in which people strike their own facial bones, typically with a hammer or similar object, in the belief that the resulting trauma will remodel the bone into a more defined, "chiselled" shape . It belongs to the bonehacks category of looksmaxxing.
claims: Hitting facial bones makes them grow or reshape ("it works").
Visible changes are caused by bonesmashing rather than puberty or other factors.

name: Jawline hammer tools
summary: Hammers and similar tools for striking the face to reshape bone; untested in studies, with surgeons warning of fractures and nerve injury.
lead: Jawline hammer tools, also called face hammers, are hammers or similar implements marketed or discussed for striking the face and jaw in the belief that doing so reshapes bone. They are associated with bonesmashing, a looksmaxxing practice in which people hit their facial bones in the hope of remodeling them .
